themes_detail.label: Curb condition crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints exploded to 15 this week versus a baseline of 1.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 900% spike (z-score: 9.55)—suggesting a sudden, widespread deterioration in street infrastructure across Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 15 curb condition complaints this week vs. 1.5 per week baseline (900% increase)
Z-score of 9.55 indicates statistically rare event
District has standing budget request for street reconstruction via DOT
Aligns with consistently high street condition complaints (2,377 total over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Ground-truth inspection: photograph curb damage across neighborhood to confirm severity and geographic pattern
Interview residents about safety hazards (wheelchairs, strollers, elderly pedestrians) and economic impact
Track whether spike correlates with recent weather event, street work, or deferred maintenance cycle

themes_detail.label: Street signage vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs spiked to 6 complaints this week versus a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 586% increase (z-score: 4.87)—while damaged street signs hit 6 complaints 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 1.6 per week (269% increase), pointing to systematic infrastructure failure affecting pedestrian and traffic safety.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints this week vs. 0.9 per week baseline (586% increase, z-score: 4.87)
6 damaged street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 per week baseline (269% increase, z-score: 5.11)
Combined signal: 12 sign-related complaints in 2-week window
Community board requests code enforcement expansion year over year (unsolved problem)
reporting_angles: Map the geographic distribution of missing/damaged signs—are specific corridors or intersections affected?
Interview DOT about maintenance schedules and whether staffing cuts explain the spike
Document safety impact: illegal turns, pedestrian confusion, accident risk at intersections

themes_detail.label: Noise complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints reached 71 this week versus a baseline of 42.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 66% spike (z-score: 4.78)—indicating a meaningful acceleration in quality-of-life issues for residents.
evidence: 71 residential noise complaints this week vs. 42.9 per week baseline (66% increase, z-score: 4.78)
Noise ranks 7th in overall complaint volume across 90-day period (618 complaints)
Sustained elevated baseline suggests chronic issue with new acute spike
reporting_angles: Interview residents about noise sources (construction, late-night vendors, traffic, bars/entertainment venues)
Check whether spike correlates with specific event, weather change, or new commercial activity
Investigate NYPD noise enforcement data and response times in district

themes_detail.label: Illegal posting proliferation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 4 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting possible organized poster activity or gang marking in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 per week baseline (967% increase, z-score: 7.49)
Community board requests code enforcement expansion annually
May signal organized poster activity or gang territory marking
reporting_angles: Document what is being posted: gang tags, political material, advertisements? Photograph locations.
Interview community board and local precinct about enforcement response and whether pattern is organized
Check whether spike correlates with removal efforts elsewhere in the city (displacement effect)

themes_detail.label: Air quality deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints reached 6 this week versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% spike (z-score: 3.96)—raising questions about new pollution sources, construction activity, or environmental hazards affecting neighborhood residents.
evidence: 6 air quality complaints this week vs. 1.2 per week baseline (380% increase, z-score: 3.96)
Asbestos complaints also spiked 3 weeks ago (3 vs. 0.4 baseline, 700% increase)
Combined signal suggests potential construction-related environmental hazard
623 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (69 new buildings, 15 full demolitions)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference air quality spike with active DOB demolitions and new construction permits—potential asbestos or dust hazard
Interview DEP about air quality monitoring data and any known pollution sources (trucking, industrial, idling vehicles)
Document resident health complaints and whether spike correlates with specific construction project timeline
